goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points to the same bug: cacheMu was narrowed, so concurrent BuildIndex calls can build the same index twice.

goldens.comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points to the same race: TotalDocs iterates the cache without a lock while the watcher goroutine can trigger a BuildIndex write.

candidates: Duplicate index builds allowed: bleveBackend.BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu across the build, so concurrent callers building the same key can both build separate indexes and then race to store into b.cache (last writer wins), wasting work, leaving one built index untracked, and for file-backed indexes can cause concurrent creation/writes to the same directory

TotalDocs map race panic: searchSupport.init calls s.search.TotalDocs() after starting a WatchWriteEvents goroutine; if an event triggers a cache write while TotalDocs iterates the cache map, the process can panic with 'concurrent map iteration and map write' during startup because bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates over the cache map without any lock while BuildIndex writes to the same map
